args.sql: SELECT MIN(event_time), MAX(event_time), MIN(signup_date), MAX(signup_date), COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT usr_id) FROM users_data
SELECT MIN(event_time), MAX(event_time), MIN(signup_date), MAX(signup_date), COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM users_data

WITH u AS (SELECT user_id, MIN(signup_date) sd, COUNT(DISTINCT signup_date) nsd FROM users_data GROUP BY user_id),
e AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.user_id, CAST(julianday(date(d.event_time)) - julianday(u.sd) AS INT) dd FROM users_data d JOIN u USING(user_id))
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM u WHERE nsd>1) multi_signup, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM e WHERE dd<0) pre_signup_events, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM u WHERE sd BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30') q3_users

WITH u AS (SELECT user_id, MIN(signup_date) sd FROM users_data GROUP BY user_id HAVING sd BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'),
e AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.user_id, CAST(julianday(date(d.event_time)) - julianday(u.sd) AS INT) dd FROM users_data d JOIN u USING(user_id)),
f AS (SELECT u.user_id, substr(u.sd,1,7) cohort,
 MAX(CASE WHEN dd=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) d1,
 MAX(CASE WHEN dd BETWEEN 1 AND 7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) w1,
 MAX(CASE WHEN dd BETWEEN 8 AND 14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) w2,
 MAX(CASE WHEN dd BETWEEN 22 AND 28 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) w4
 FROM u LEFT JOIN e USING(user_id) GROUP BY u.user_id)
SELECT cohort, COUNT(*) users, SUM(d1) d1_n, ROUND(100.0*AVG(d1),1) d1_pct, SUM(w1) w1_n, ROUND(100.0*AVG(w1),1) w1_pct, SUM(w2) w2_n, ROUND(100.0*AVG(w2),1) w2_pct, SUM(w4) w4_n, ROUND(100.0*AVG(w4),1) w4_pct
FROM f GROUP BY cohort
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Q3 2026 total', COUNT(*), SUM(d1), ROUND(100.0*AVG(d1),1), SUM(w1), ROUND(100.0*AVG(w1),1), SUM(w2), ROUND(100.0*AVG(w2),1), SUM(w4), ROUND(100.0*AVG(w4),1) FROM f

args.text:
*Retention – Q3 2026 signup cohorts* (354 users who signed up Jul–Sep 2026)

• Day 1: *33.1%*
• Week 1 (days 1–7): *97.7%*
• Week 2 (days 8–14): *61.9%*
• Week 4 (days 22–28): *49.7%*

By month, Week 4 retention was Jul 52.9%, Aug 44.9% and Sep 51.3%. August had the weakest cohort. Early retention held steady across all three months.
A user counts as retained if they had any event in the window. Source: `users_data`.
Full breakdown: https://sheets.example.com/sh1

finalText:
I calculated retention for the users who signed up last quarter, put the results in a new spreadsheet and posted a summary with the link to #analytics.

**How I counted it:**
- **Last quarter** means Q3 2026 (July to September), the last complete quarter. The data runs until 11 Nov 2026.
- **Users counted:** the 354 people who signed up in Q3, grouped by signup month.
- **Retained** means the user did anything (logged in, viewed a page or made a purchase) in that period after signing up. Every period has fully passed, so no group is undercounted.

| Signup month | Users | Day 1 | Week 1 (days 1–7) | Week 2 (days 8–14) | Week 4 (days 22–28) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jul 2026 | 121 | 31.4% | 97.5% | 62.8% | 52.9% |
| Aug 2026 | 118 | 30.5% | 97.5% | 61.9% | 44.9% |
| Sep 2026 | 115 | 37.4% | 98.3% | 60.9% | 51.3% |
| **Q3 total** | **354** | **33.1%** | **97.7%** | **61.9%** | **49.7%** |

About half of new users were still active in their fourth week. The August group did worst by then, at 44.9%. Retention in the first two weeks was steady across all three months.

The table's built-in description lists the user column as `usr_id`, but it's actually called `user_id`. You might want to fix that description.

Spreadsheet: https://sheets.example.com/sh1
